  1. vLLM on GPU

vLLM on GPU

Standard single-node LLM serving with an OpenAI-compatible API. This is the usual production starting point.

Complete values file 

namespace: models

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

components:
  llmisvcCrd:
    enabled: true
  llmisvc:
    enabled: true

llmDefaults:
  replicas: 1
  image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
  args:
    - --model
    - /mnt/models
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "8"
      memory: 32Gi

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
      name: llama-3.1-8b-instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --served-model-name
      - llama-3.1-8b-instruct
      - --max-model-len
      - "8192"
      - --dtype
      - bfloat16
      - --gpu-memory-utilization
      - "0.90"
    replicas: 2
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

Create the token Secret, then install:

kubectl create namespace models
kubectl create secret generic hf-secret -n models --from-literal=HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN"

helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve --create-namespace -f gpu-values.yaml

Serving several models 

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --max-model-len
      - "8192"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

  - name: mistral-7b
    model:
      uri: hf://mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --max-model-len
      - "16384"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

  - name: qwen-14b
    model:
      uri: hf://Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "2"
      - --max-model-len
      - "8192"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "16"
        memory: 64Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

Quantized models

Quantization fits larger models on smaller GPUs at some quality cost.

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-70b-awq
    model:
      uri: hf://hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4
    args:
      - --model
      - /mnt/models
      - --quantization
      - awq
      - --tensor-parallel-size
      - "2"
      - --max-model-len
      - "4096"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "16"
        memory: 96Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "2"

Common vLLM arguments

Argument Purpose
--served-model-name Name clients pass in the model field
--max-model-len Context window; the strongest memory lever
--gpu-memory-utilization Fraction of GPU memory to use, typically 0.85–0.95
--tensor-parallel-size GPUs per replica; must equal the GPU limit
--dtype bfloat16, float16, or auto
--quantization awq, gptq, fp8
--enable-chunked-prefill Improves throughput with long prompts
--max-num-seqs Concurrent sequence cap
--enforce-eager Disables CUDA graphs; lowers memory, reduces speed

Alternative: the models list

For a simple single-node deployment, the classic list also works and uses the upstream runtime:

models:
  - name: llama-8b-isvc
    runtime: kserve-vllmserver
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia-a100
    tolerations:
      - key: nvidia.com/gpu
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 4
    scaleMetric: concurrency
    scaleTarget: 80
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 32Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: 48Gi
        nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

The models list renders scheduling and scaling fields directly, which llmInferenceServices does not. Choose llmInferenceServices when you need routing, multi-node, disaggregation, or LLM-aware autoscaling.

Verify 

kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models
kubectl get pods -n models -w
kubectl logs -n models -l app.kubernetes.io/name=llama-8b --tail=100

kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3.1-8b-instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about storage."}],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0.7
  }'

Watch GPU use:

kubectl exec -n models deploy/llama-8b -- nvidia-smi
